Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioners / accused Nos.1 to 3 are before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.120/2022 of Kalaburagi City Women Police Station, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 109 r/w Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for short 'D.P. Act'), pending on the file of learned I Addl.
Civil Judge (Jr. Dn.) & J.M.F.C. at Kalaburagi.
2. Heard Shri Ashok Mulage, learned counsel for the petitioners and Shri Nandkishore Boob,
learned counsel for the respondent.
Perused the material on record.
Brief facts of the case are:-
3. It is the case of the complainant that the complainant married petitioner No.1 on 15.10.2021.
It was registered before the Sub-Registrar Office, Kalaburagi on 27.10.2021.

After the marriage,
petitioner No.1 was staying with the complainant in her house and thereafter, he went to his native.
Whenever it is being demanded to the petitioner No.1 to take the complainant to his place, it is alleged that petitioner No.1 used to demand dowry.
The parents of the complainant had paid Rs.7 lakhs and 5 tholas of gold to petitioner No.1 at the time of marriage.
In spite of having received the dowry at the time of marriage, it is alleged that the petitioner No.1 again demanded Rs.2.5 lakhs.
The said demand was also fulfilled.
However, the complainant was not taken to her matrimonial house.
It is further alleged that again the petitioners collectively demanding Rs.12 lakhs from the complainant to receive her to the matrimonial home.

It is alleged that on 10.11.2022 at about 10-30 p.m. when the complainant and her parents were in the house, the petitioner No.1 came to the house of the complainant and forced her to sign the divorce papers.

When she refused to give the consent,
he assaulted and scolded her in front of her parents and other witnesses.
After the incident, the complainant had gone to the Government Hospital on 12.11.2022 and obtained treatment for the injuries which she had sustained in the incident.
As such, the complainant filed a complaint before the jurisdictional police and the police have registered the case in Crime No.120/2022 for the above said offences.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are innocent of the alleged offences.
The learned counsel further submitted that the alleged offences are neither punishable with death nor imprisonment for life.
The petitioner No.1 is working in Army at Gauhati and he is earning member of the family and the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are parents of the petitioner No.1.
They are the permanent residents of Vishnunagar, Near Gayathri Chow Arra, Bhojapur, Bihar and they are aged persons.

The entire allegations are made against the petitioner No.1 only, however,
petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are also falsely implicated as accused in this case in order to harass them.

It is Vijaykumar S/O Pramodkumarray And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132840207/
2 further stated that even though the allegedly taken place on 10.11.2022, on that day, the petitioner No.1 was in Bhojpur, Bihar and he has been falsely implicated in this case in order to harass him.

sentences.text: In fact, on 03.11.2022, petitioner No.1 had filed divorce petition before Bhojpur, Bihar and to counter blast the same, a false case has been registered against the petitioners.
As such, learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

5. Sri.Nandkishore Boob, learned counsel for the complainant / respondent filed detailed objection and narrated the entire facts and the way in which the marriage had taken place etc., and submitted that the petitioner No.1 deliberately and intentionally married respondent No.1 in order to escape from the clutches of law and thereafter, the petitioners started ill-treating her and not even bothered to take her to the matrimonial home after the marriage.

Petitioner No.1 had assaulted the complainant and kicked her stomach when she was pregnant and on 12.11.2022, she was admitted to GIMS Hospital, Kalaburagi for treatment and it is stated that, miscarriage had taken place.

The learned counsel draw the attention of this Court to the medical certificate and its contents, which reads thus:
"H/o of P/v per original bleeding followed by Assault.
O/E ISSG - Abdomen & Pelvis - within normal limits.
OPINION: I am of the opinion that above injury is simple in nature caused by hand & blunt object a/c of injury is within 6 cms."
Considering the severity of the assault made by petitioner No.1, all the petitioners are not entitled for any relief as sought in the petition.

6. Similarly, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition and submitted the statement of the witnesses, wherein some of the witnesses have stated that the petitioner No.1 assaulted the complainant indiscriminately and brutally on 10.11.2022 in the house of the complainant and it is stated that, on hearing the commotion, witnesses went to the house of the complainant and pacified the quarrel.

It is further submitted that, since the offences involved are heinous in nature, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
7.
Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the documents on record.
8. It is relevant to refer the averments of the complaint before adverting into the merits of the case.
It is stated in the complaint that the complainant married petitioner No.1 and both were living in the house of her parents for shorter period.
Thereafter, petitioner No.1 left the company of the complainant and gone to the place of work.

It is stated in the complaint, in spite of repeated demands made to petitioner No.1 to take her to matrimonial home, on one or other pretext he was refusing to take her to the matrimonial home and it is stated in the complaint that he was demanding huge amount as dowry.
9. On careful reading of the complaint and also averments of the petition, it is noticed that petitioner No.1 had filed divorce petition in Bhojpur which is numbered as M.C.No.445/2022 on 03.11.2022.

10. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioners are ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of their arrest in Crime No.120/2022 of Kalaburagi City Women Police Station, pending on the file of learned I Addl.
Civil Judge (Jr. Dn.) & J.M.F.C. at Kalaburagi.

sentences.text:
The petitioners are directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order and on their appearance, the Investigating Officer shall enlarge them on bail, subject to the following conditions:-
a.

The petitioners shall furnish the personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) each with one surety each for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Investigating Officer.

b. The petitioners shall co-operate with the investigation and they shall appear before the Investigating Officer, as and when it is required for the purpose of investigation,
upon receiving notice under section 41-A of Cr.P.C. by the Investigating Officer.
c.
The petitioners may take the assistance of Advocate to appear before the Investigating Officer, when their presence is required for investigation.
d. The petitioners shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing.
If in case, the petitioners did not co-operate with the investigation, liberty is reserved to the complainant and the Investigating Officer to file appropriate application for cancellation of bail.
